# gatekeep-pr #42: deliver-nits course, from the retained pick to the final menu

**Tracker.** The tracker was initialized at invocation start with `gather, provision, verify`. There was no `--rebase`, so there is no `sync` stage. The first task's name carries `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. During this loop, each re-entered stage is re-opened and `add`ed only when it starts: `review` after each own push, then `report`, then `menu`.

## Entry: validate the retained course

1. **Validate the run record.**
   - Read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`.
   - It matches `consent.target`: `acme/widgets`, PR `42`, base `main`.
   - The stored course is `deliver-nits`, set by the human's numeric pick at the prior initial menu. Caps are 10/10 (2 x maxFixRounds 5) and usage is 0/0.
2. **Fetch the target state.**
   - Run `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,body,baseRefName`.
   - Head is `1111111`, state is OPEN, the body is unchanged, and the live base `main` equals the consent base.
3. **Exit check.**
   - Every merge precondition holds at `1111111`.
   - Readiness still fails: under deliver-nits it needs a `resolved` closure line for every opted-in nit, and N1 and N2 are open.
   - There is no obstacle and no cap hit, so the D3 body runs and no menu renders.

## D3 iteration 1 (head 1111111)

4. **Prepare the wave.**
   - Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "closureReview" })`: maxFixRounds is 5, and the caps stay 10/10.
   - Persist `repair.wave`:
     - `pre_wave_head` 1111111
     - `round_start_head` 1111111
     - `counted: false`
     - `stage: apply`
     - `selected_ids` N1 and N2 with their payload snapshots
5. **Check for base conflicts.**
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 fetch origin main`
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0.
   - The PR is MERGEABLE and CLEAN, so Loop sync is not triggered.
6. **Resolve the scoped test command.** `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS` resolves from the merge-base config to `node --test src/guard.test.mjs`.
7. **Dispatch the N1 implementer.** One fresh `implementer`, `cwd /work/widgets-pr-42`. Its task carries:
   - N1's evidence pack: remove the unused import at `src/guard.mjs:1`. The helper applies that payload and never re-solves the finding.
   - The smallest in-repo edit only: no infrastructure, dependency, or module.
   - `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS`, and the full suite is not run.
   - The commit rule: one commit only if the scoped test passes, otherwise discard its edits and return `open - <why>`.
   - The report shape: the failing run before the edit and the passing run after it.
   - The stored scope baseline, with the rule to return `open - contract exception` rather than make a contract-changing commit.

   The helper returns `done`. `git -C … status --porcelain` is clean, and `git -C … rev-parse HEAD` shows exactly one new commit.
   - Persist `counted: true`, `counted_head`, and `rounds_used` 1.
8. **Dispatch the N2 implementer.** It is the same kind of fresh `implementer` with the same rules, for the duplicate guard at `src/guard.mjs:6`.
   - It returns `done` with one new commit and a clean tree.
   - This is the same round, so no extra round is counted.
9. **Run the pre-push review** (stage `review`).
   - One fresh `code-reviewer`, `cwd /work/widgets-pr-42`, read-only, over `1111111..HEAD`.
   - Its task carries:
     - N1 and N2 under `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`
     - `git diff 1111111 HEAD` under `## Fix delta`
     - the closure-line contract
   - It returns `N1: resolved` and `N2: resolved` with no new findings. The carried set is empty.
10. **Pre-push checks.**
    - Rerun `merge-tree`: it exits 0.
    - Run the compare-and-swap read: `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. Head is still `1111111`, the body and base are unchanged.
    - Run the output done-check on the commit subjects.
11. **Push** (stage `push`).
    - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:acme/widgets.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/guard`
    - The head becomes `2222222`.
    - Persist `repair.wave.pushed_head` and the digest `headRefOid` as `2222222`. `poll_deadline` is null, so there is nothing to renew.
12. **D3 step 4, Wait course.**
    - Classify checks on `2222222`: ci / test is completed SUCCESS and there is no binding pending check.
    - Skip `gh pr checks --watch`, so no deadline is minted.
13. **Own-push Re-render.**
    - Run the pre-menu refresh:
      - `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,…,mergeCommit`
      - `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 2222222… --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
    - Evidence is CI-sufficient on `2222222` (ci / test).
    - Claim dispositions carry to the pushed SHA. No claim-check helper runs, because no claim is pending and no description was written.
    - Re-fetch comments with `gh api …/pulls/42/comments --paginate` and `gh api …/issues/42/comments --paginate`. No reviewer workflow is known, so no reviewer `gh run list` runs.
    - Diff the comment ledger, then do Section C triage.
    - The fresh comment source review runs as one fresh `code-reviewer`, `cwd` the worktree, at `2222222`, against the merge-base rubric.
      - It finds N3: an unused helper at `src/guard.mjs:20`.
      - This is a Minor finding, so it becomes a nit and is minted as a new append-only ID.
    - Replace the digest `comments` with the fresh set.
    - Close `repair.wave` after reconciliation.
14. **Exit check.** Every merge precondition holds. Under deliver-nits, the newly minted N3 has no closure line, so readiness fails and the loop continues with no menu.

## D3 iteration 2 (head 2222222)

15. **Prepare the wave.**
    - Persist a new `repair.wave`: `pre_wave_head` and `round_start_head` 2222222, `counted: false`, `selected_ids` N3.
    - Run `git -C … fetch origin main`, then `merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`: it exits 0, so there is no sync.
16. **Dispatch the N3 implementer.** A fresh `implementer` with `cwd` the worktree and the same task rules as above, for the unused helper at `src/guard.mjs:20`.
    - It returns `done` with one new commit, a clean tree, and the scoped test passing.
    - Persist `counted: true` and `rounds_used` 2.
17. **Run the pre-push review.**
    - A fresh read-only `code-reviewer` over `2222222..HEAD`, with N3 as the re-review trigger, the fix delta `git diff 2222222 HEAD`, and closure lines.
    - It returns `N3: resolved` with no new finding.
18. **Pre-push checks.**
    - Rerun `merge-tree`: it exits 0.
    - Run the compare-and-swap `gh pr view`: head is still `2222222`, the body and base are unchanged.
    - Run the done-check on the commit subject.
19. **Push.**
    - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:acme/widgets.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/guard`
    - The head becomes `3333333`. Persist `pushed_head` and `headRefOid` as `3333333`.
20. **Wait course.** ci / test is SUCCESS on `3333333` and there is no binding pending check, so the watch call is skipped.
21. **Re-render.**
    - Run the pre-menu refresh: `gh pr view …` plus `gh run list -c 3333333…`. Evidence is CI-sufficient on `3333333`.
    - Re-fetch comments with both `--paginate` calls. The last re-review has no nit or blocker. Replace the comments.
    - Close the wave.
22. **Exit check, readiness.**
    - All of these hold:
      - every blocker is fixed
      - N1, N2 and N3 are resolved
      - CI evidence exists on the assessed head, with provenance clean
      - MERGEABLE / CLEAN, with no failing or binding pending check
      - the worktree is tracked-clean and synced to the remote
    - Read the merge policy: `gh api repos/acme/widgets --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge}'` returns `allow_squash_merge` true.
    - This exits to readiness, and the final template renders. The `report` and then `menu` stages are added and closed.

**Assessed SHA:** verification evidence and the brief both assess `3333333333333333333333333333333333333333`.

**Sync line:** none renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

## Final report and menu

```
Delivers: the PR rejects unsigned events.

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (ci / test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge PR 42 into main at 3333333. [recommended]
2. stop - end the run and leave the PR and its checkout as they are.

Not offered: approve (your own PR)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

The narration stops here, with no merge pick.

The invocation's initial tracker stages are `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`, with `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` in the first task's name. There is no `sync` stage because the arguments contain no `--rebase`. At this Entry checkpoint I do not initialize another tracker or repeat completed assessment.

Verification and the original brief assess `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. Its exact-head CI evidence and material-claim dispositions are already established.

Although the source head satisfies the merge prerequisites, `deliver-nits` has two unresolved opted-in nits. The Exit check therefore does not return readiness. I continue delivery without rendering a menu.

In the commands below, `$WT` is `/work/widgets-pr-42`. Variables for helper output files receive the paths returned by their respective `mktemp` commands. Intermediate local commit SHAs are recorded from command output, not invented.

## First delivery iteration

I add the active delivery stage to the tracker, persist `pre_wave_head` as the gathered head, and initialize the wave's round checkpoint with `counted: false`. I retain the concrete payloads for removing the unused import and duplicate guard.

I run, in order:

```sh
git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "$WT" fetch origin main
git -C "$WT" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
```

The conflict check is clean. Neither the forge state nor the local conflict check triggers sync.

### Remove the unused import

I run:

```sh
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a fresh, synchronous **implementer**, with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`, and its own output path.

Its task carries:

- The assessed scope baseline and the concrete unused-import payload for `src/guard.mjs:1`.
- The requirement to check the task's current wave HEAD before working.
- Exactly `node --test src/guard.test.mjs` as its scoped test command, with the failing-before and passing-after results reported.

The helper runs its scoped checks, removes the import, commits the fix, and returns `done`. I read its result, then run:

```sh
git -C "$WT" status --porcelain
git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD
```

There is exactly one new commit and a clean tree. I persist `counted: true`, the resulting head, and `rounds_used: 1`.

### Remove the duplicate guard

I run:

```sh

```

I dispatch a second fresh, synchronous **implementer**, with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42` and a separate output path.

Its task carries the same execution, testing, restoration, commit, scope, and output rules, now targeting only the duplicate guard at `src/guard.mjs:6` and checking the current wave HEAD.

The helper runs the scoped checks, removes the duplicate guard, commits the fix, and returns `done`. I read its result, then run:

```sh
git -C "$WT" status --porcelain
git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD
```

There is exactly one additional commit and a clean tree. This is still the same repair round, so usage remains 1 of 10.

### Review before the first push

I add the review stage when it starts and run:

```sh

mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a fresh, synchronous **code-reviewer**, with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`, read-only.

It must return its native report plus one `resolved` or `open - <why>` closure line for each dispatched finding. It must not edit, commit, or push.

### First push

```sh

git -C "$WT" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
git -C "$WT" push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:acme/widgets.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/guard
```

The remote head, body, and base still match the expected snapshot; the conflict check is clean. The push succeeds. I persist the pushed and assessed head as `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`.

This is an ordinary push, not a rewrite. No lease push, rebase, or sync accounting applies.

## Reconcile the first pushed head

I run the pre-menu refresh, which is also the first step of own-push reconciliation:


CI is successful on this exact pushed head. I bind the report to that evidence and the pre-push closure lines. I do not rerun the full verification command, perform a whole-wave review, or repeat the already-dispositioned material claims.

At delivery step 4, no binding check is pending, so I run no watch and create no watch deadline.

I then run the comment reads:

I reconcile the fresh comment identities and bodies with the retained ledger. No known reviewer workflow requires a run-list query, and no placeholder requires a run-view query.

It must treat the comment as a lead, verify the concern against source, and return its native findings report. It must not run a full suite or review the whole diff solely because a comment changed.

The source review finds the unused helper at `src/guard.mjs:20`. I integrate it as a new nit, retain its evidence and concrete payload, and update the comment baseline only after source review completes.

I complete reconciliation of the first wave. Usage is 1 of 10 rounds and 0 of 10 syncs.

The persistent `deliver-nits` course includes this newly minted nit. The Exit check therefore continues delivery without a menu.

## Second delivery iteration

I persist a new wave checkpoint with `pre_wave_head` and `round_start_head` equal to `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`, and `counted: false`.

I run:

### Review before the second push

```sh
git -C "$WT" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
```

Freshness and conflict checks pass. The push succeeds. I persist the pushed and assessed head as `3333333333333333333333333333333333333333`.

## Final reconciliation and readiness

I run:

```sh
gh pr view 42 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
```

I run the remaining readiness checks:

The final report assesses `3333333333333333333333333333333333333333`, using exact-head CI evidence and the own-push review closure lines. No full Verify or whole-diff Review helper is rerun after either own push.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers all three facts that Before missed: it treats the retained deliver-nits course as standing authority (Before explicitly rejected the course as 'not a grant this skill recognizes' and rendered final with N1/N2 take-or-leave), dispatches fresh N1 and N2 implementers, re-reviews to resolved lines, pushes to 2222222, mints N3 from the fresh comment source review and folds it into iteration 2 without a menu, then reaches final at 3333333 only after N3: resolved, exact-head CI evidence and reconciliation, with merge offered but not executed. Nothing regressed relative to Before. Two small tightenings would make f3 unambiguous rather than inferred: have the final section state outright that `course` is still `deliver-nits` in the record (After only implies it by never switching), and keep the Before-style 'nits open' / closure accounting visible in the final report (e.g. 'Nits: N1, N2, N3 resolved') so a reader can see the readiness condition met in the rendered text, not only in the preceding exit-check bullets.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves all three facts to holds: it treats the retained deliver-nits course as persistent authority, so the already-mergeable head still gets both N1 and N2 implementers in the first wave instead of exiting readiness, the N3 nit minted by the comment-source review at 2222222 is folded into the next wave without a menu or new pick, and the final menu is rendered only after reviewer closure lines for all three nits, exact-head CI success on 3333333, and tracked-clean/HEAD checks, with merge left as a separate numeric selection. Before failed every fact because it read deliver-nits as a spent one-shot `fix nits` grant and rendered the final menu with N1/N2 still open. One wording nit for the After template: the final section never explicitly restates that the course remains `deliver-nits` after reconciliation (it is only implied by 'persistent course' earlier and the absence of any reset); adding a one-line persisted-state summary at the final menu (e.g. 'course: deliver-nits, rounds 2/10, syncs 0/10') would make f3's course-retention clause unambiguous without affecting the Change.
